decision: Whether to accept a 6-month internship offer
details: Good stipend, close to home, working hours 9-5, role in software development, learning opportunities include industry tools, college schedule has classes Monday-Thursday
reasons: Mainly considering it because the stipend is good, the company is close to home, and it will provide industry experience

overlooked_factors.text: Impact on academic performance and college schedule balance
overlooked_factors.why_it_matters: The internship during academic term could affect grades, course comprehension, and ability to participate in campus activities

overlooked_factors.text: Quality and accessibility of mentorship in the role
overlooked_factors.why_it_matters: Industry experience varies greatly depending on mentorship quality - poor mentorship could limit learning despite the prestigious company name

overlooked_factors.text: Long-term career alignment with personal goals
overlooked_factors.why_it_matters: Software development experience may not align with evolving career interests, potentially creating a skills mismatch for future goals

assumptions.text: Good stipend automatically means the opportunity is worthwhile
assumptions.how_to_test: Calculate actual hourly rate after taxes and compare to other opportunities; consider what the stipend doesn't cover (transportation, meals, etc.)

assumptions.text: Close to home means low cost and minimal inconvenience
assumptions.how_to_test: Map out actual commute time and costs; consider time value of that commute versus other uses

assumptions.text: Any industry experience is valuable regardless of specific role or tasks
assumptions.how_to_test: Research specific tasks and projects involved; talk to current or former interns about day-to-day work

conflicts.statement_a: I want to gain valuable industry experience for my career
conflicts.statement_b: I'm choosing based primarily on stipend and proximity rather than learning opportunities
conflicts.tension: There's a potential mismatch between stated career goals and actual decision drivers

conflicts.statement_a: My college schedule and academic performance are important to me
conflicts.statement_b: I'm considering an internship that takes place during the academic term
conflicts.tension: The timing of the internship may conflict with academic priorities

questions.text: What specific evidence would convince you that the stipend truly represents good value for your time?
How would you evaluate the actual quality of mentorship and learning opportunities available in this role?
If you had to choose between maximizing stipend and maximizing learning quality, which would you prioritize and why?
How might your feelings about this decision change in 6 months, 1 year, or 5 years from now?
Who else besides yourself might be affected by this decision, and what might their perspectives be?
